chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn Uqba from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Sometimes the Hajj eludes me, so I will go to be a pilgrim (mu'arrif) at the grave of Husayn, recognizing his right.' He said: 'Well done, O Bashir. Any believer who visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, on a day other than Eid, Allah will write for him twenty Hajj pilgrimages and twenty Umrahs, all accepted and accepted, and twenty battles with a Messenger Prophet or an upright Imam. And whoever visits him on the day of Eid, Allah will write for him one hundred Hajj pilgrimages, one hundred Umrahs, and one hundred battles with a Messenger Prophet or an upright Imam.'

I said: 'And how can I attain such a standing?' He looked at me as if slightly angry, then said: 'O Bashir, indeed when a believer visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Arafah, and performs ritual bath (ghusl) from the Euphrates, then turns towards it, Allah writes for him for every step a Hajj with all its rituals.' And I do not know except that he said: 'And an Umrah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn's grave on the Day of 'Arafah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the grave of Imam Husayn (peace be upon him) as a spiritual substitute for the Prophet’s grave, granting rewards equivalent to twenty or one hundred Hajj pilgrimages depending on the timing. The specific mention of bathing in the Euphrates (*al-Furat*) before visiting on the Day of 'Arafah underscores the unique geographical and ritual significance of the Karbala shrine within Shia devotional practice, linking the martyrdom of the Imam to the culmination of the Hajj season.
